column1: # POOT-1143 stages 2 and 3: device times of the block top-k and selected-attention kernels.
# POOT-1166: the block top-k rows below are re-measured after the packed-count radix select (7 passes of 5 bits, or
# 8 of 4, down from 11 of 3; kernelgen/src/block_top_k.rs). wgpu 32768 blocks: median 1862.8 -> 219.4 us, floor 1494.9 -> 210.2.
# rocm 32768 blocks: floor 289.3 -> 133.6 us, median 1389.5 -> 1499.4 (the rocm rows are noisy between holds). The
# paragraph on "11 passes" below describes the state before POOT-1166. The other rows are unchanged from POOT-1143.
# Produced by `block_top_k_and_selected_attention_device_times` (poot-wgpu-device and poot-rocm-device,
# tests/selected_attention_receipt.rs) on the Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151), device timestamps (never host wall),
# fixtures interleaved A B / B A over 4 rounds of 8 steps, the first step of every visit dropped: 32 samples.
# Columns: backend, fixture, median_us, min_us, max_us, samples.
# The box is shared (desktop, other lanes' non-GPU-locked work): single numbers move ~30% between holds and the
# spread here is wider. Read the min as the kernel's floor and the median as what a step sees.
# What it says against the design (flash-next-qsa-depth.md section 4.2):
# - The design claimed a 3-pass radix select (12/12/8 bits, 4096 bins) at ~10-30 us per row. The kernel here is
#   11 passes (2 + 10x3 bits) that each re-read the row from global memory: LLVM's SPIR-V backend miscompiles
#   the workgroup atomic a histogram needs (see kernelgen/src/block_top_k.rs), so each lane counts into a row of
#   its own, and a 4096-bin table does not fit the 16 KiB of workgroup memory a Vulkan device guarantees.
#   At 32768 blocks (128K positions) it takes ~1.4-1.9 ms median (0.29-1.5 ms floor) per layer call: about 50-150x the
#   design figure (the floor is ~10-30x), so twelve layers spend ~17-22 ms of a decode step in the selection.
# - It scales with the row (2048 -> 32768 blocks: ~5x on the floor, ~6x on the median), as 11 passes over a
#   resident row should; nothing quadratic is left.
# - The selected attention does not scale with depth (32K -> 128K positions: rocm 1.1 -> 1.8 ms median, wgpu
#   14.5 -> 13.8 ms) and is ~12x (32K) and ~48x (128K) faster than the dense attention over the same cache on
#   rocm (21.9 and 84.7 ms median). wgpu's dense row is timed at 32K only: the 128K dense dispatch lost the RADV
#   context on this box ("context is lost ... guilty of a hard recovery"); the selected row at 128K ran.
# - wgpu runs the selected attention ~10x slower than rocm (14 vs 1.1-1.8 ms): its 16 KiB of workgroup memory
#   leaves few lanes per row (attention_lanes), so each lane walks many candidates serially.
# Before the split-KV rule divided the candidates, wgpu took 51 ms for the selected row.
# Not run: PTX (no NVIDIA device on this box). poot-ptx-device/tests/selected_attention_receipt.rs is the same row.
